messages:
megan (sales): Hey team — enterprise prospect (FinLedger) is asking for a committed plan. They want predictable 99th p95 latency for chat generation at sustained peak of ~220 rps and occasional spikes to 1.2k rps for 10–15 min. What reservation + autoscale runway do we recommend?

alex (eng-platform): Thanks, megan. Quick clarifying Qs: what's the typical prompt length / average output tokens per request for their profile? And which model family are they evaluating?

lina (solutions): FinLedger said average prompt ~120 tokens and completion ~180 tokens. They're testing with an Llama-2-70b-ish open variant quantized to int8. Concurrency per GPU (gen path) roughly 10 concurrent streams for 2k token windows in our benchmarking but that's for extreme cases.

megan (sales): They'd prefer we size for the L2-70b quantized baseline. They also asked about prewarm and burst credits during payroll cycle spikes.

alex (eng-platform): OK — rough math: if one quantized 70b GPU supports ~80–100 rps for short 300-token hops (our bench shows ~90 rps sustained with batching). But for chat with longer cache reuse, effective sustained rps drops. For safety, plan 10–12 concurrent requests per GPU for their mix.

alex (eng-platform): Proposed reservation: baseline reserved pool of 12 GPUs to cover steady 220 rps (12 GPUs * ~18 rps each ≈ 216 rps conservative). Add a burst runway: 40 GPUs on standby as burst capacity (hot standby or fast-prewarm) to handle spikes to 1.2k rps. That gives runway with autoscale policy to bring replicas online within ~90s.

tom (eng-sre): Two operational notes: 1) Prewarming KV cache matters — cold-start can cost ~2–3x latency tokens for first few requests. 2) Autoscale cooldowns should be tuned aggressively for these short payroll spikes: scale-up cooldown 20s, scale-down cooldown 10m to avoid thrash.

lina (solutions): For pricing, if they want monthly reserved commitment we can do 12 GPUs guaranteed + metered burst usage billing for the extra GPUs during spikes. Suggest a burst_credit bucket of 600 GPU-minutes/day for scheduled spikes and extra pay-as-you-go beyond that.

megan (sales): Can we draft a concrete SLA-friendly config I can send? They want prewarm guarantees and a fallback model if capacity exhausted.

alex (eng-platform): Draft config snippet (POC recommended):

```yaml
reservation:
  reserved_gpus: 12
  burst_pool_max: 40
  burst_preheat: true
  burst_preheat_window: 5m
autoscale_policy:
  metric: rps
  target_per_gpu: 18
  min_replicas: 12
  max_replicas: 52
  scale_up_cooldown: 20s
  scale_down_cooldown: 10m
  scale_step: 8_gpus
fallbacks:
  fallback_model: llama-13b-quantized
  max_fallback_ratio: 0.15
```

alex (eng-platform): Also recommend route-based hedging: route high-priority traffic through reserved pool only, and lower-priority via public capacity to avoid reservation bleed.

tom (eng-sre): On the prewarm guarantee — we can commit to prewarm within configured burst_preheat_window for scheduled spike windows (customer provides a 10–30m heads-up webhook). For unpredictable spikes we rely on burst pool + fast scale-up; note there will be a ~60–120s ramp to full capacity for large scale events.

lina (solutions): Security Q: they asked about private model pinning and KMS. We can support model pinning on Dedicated + KMS for keys. Need to confirm EKM/HSM integration for enterprise contract.

megan (sales): Perfect. I'll share the YAML and ask them to provide typical daily spike schedules. One more: what's the expected cost uplift for holding 12 reserved GPUs + burst credits versus pure on-demand?

alex (eng-platform): Ballpark: reserved GPUs reduce per-token cost ~30–40% vs on-demand for steady usage. Adding burst credits as metered usage keeps actual committed cost lower than static overprovisioning. I'll prepare an estimate (cost/km tokens) once we get their token/day.

infra-bot: deploy-note: created reservation draft ticket #RES-4829 assigned to alex.

megan (sales): Thanks all. Action items: 1) megan -> get daily token profile and spike windows from FinLedger. 2) alex -> cost estimate and final reservation YAML + fallback playbook. 3) tom -> doc short prewarm SLA text. 4) lina -> confirm KMS/EKM path and any red-team notes. I'll loop back with the customer. :thumbsup:

alex (eng-platform): Roger. Will post cost numbers by EOD tomorrow.

tom (eng-sre): I'll draft a short runbook for the prewarm webhook and emergency manual burst (includes commands and contacts).

lina (solutions): I'll start the security checklist and ping security if EKM required.

megan (sales): Great — closing this thread for now, will reopen if FinLedger sends profile. (reacts :white_check_mark:)
